x-fake-jev.profileNote: jev/v1 is a fake-jev-owned identifier. It does not imply that TypeSafe has published an API version named jev/v1, and it is not a System One standard (§6.1, §25.4).

info.title: Jev compatibility profile (fake-jev reconstruction)
info.description: The jev/v1 data-plane surface as frozen for fake-jev. This is a protocol emulation target, not a System One standard. fake-jev emulates protocols; it does not define them (§1).

servers.description: Loopback is the default bind. An application under test switches to this by changing its base URL and nothing else (§2, §19.1).

get.summary: List the deterministic model entries exposed by the fake.
get.description: Successful response is a data-plane interaction: journaled as profile jev/v1, operation models, outcome matched, matchedStubId null, requestBody null. It requires no stub, selects none, and does not fail verification (§39.1, C-JEV-002). Authentication headers are ignored.

200.description: The model list, in configured order.

Content-Type.description: A JSON content type, possibly with a charset parameter (§39.9).

models.name: jev-latest
models.description: Local deterministic fake model provided by fake-jev.

post.summary: Submit a state and questions for a deterministic decision.
post.description: Strict mode only. An unconfigured request must not receive a plausible default: it returns HTTP 501 and fails verification (§4.6, §30.4).
post.description_note: Upstream declares bearer authentication. fake-jev MUST accept a request with no Authorization header and MUST accept any bearer token, and MUST NOT validate credentials or contact any provider in v1 (§6, §10.1, §39.5, C-JEV-017). The value MUST never be logged (§42.5).

requestBody.description: Parsed as JSON whether or not Content-Type is present or set to application/json. A non-JSON body fails with the 422 malformed-JSON envelope; v1 does not emulate strict media types (§39.6).

200.description: A matched, non-raw response. The answer map has exactly the request question-name set. JSON key order is not a protocol guarantee; golden comparisons are on parsed values (§39.4).

409.$comment: Sequence exhausted. The stub was still selected, so its invocation count incremented and stays incremented (§12.7, §40.6).
409.description: The configured response sequence is exhausted. Verification fails.

413.description: The body exceeded dataPlaneBodyBytes. Journaled as payload_too_large with requestBody null, mutates no stub state, and fails verification (§43.7, §44.15).

example.message: Request body exceeds the configured limit.

422.description: Request validation failed. The profile returns the first discovered error only, which keeps behavior deterministic without cloning upstream framework prose (§39.2).

500.description: The selected stub cannot legally answer the validated request — a missing answer, an unknown selected choice, or a helper whose type does not match the question. Detailed cause goes to stderr, not to the wire (§43.4). Verification fails. A second 500 body shape, fake_jev_internal_error, covers a fake-server internal failure (§43.6); it is listed in the same status because both are internal fake failures, and the two are distinguished by the error code.

example.message: Configured stub cannot produce a valid response for this request.

501.description: No configured stub matched. In strict mode an unconfigured decision request must not silently receive a plausible default (§4.6, §30.4). Verification fails.

example.message: No configured stub matched this request.

507.description: The journal is at maxInteractions. The request is never admitted: no sequence is assigned, no stub runs, no state mutates, and a sticky verification failure is set with requestSequence null. Older interactions are never silently evicted (§43.5, §44.14).

example.message: Interaction journal limit reached. Reset or increase maxInteractions.

bearerAuth.description: Declared by upstream and emulated as a no-op: the header is optional, any value is accepted, nothing is validated, and the value is never logged (§6, §10.1, §39.5, §42.5).

SystemOneRequest.description: Unknown fields are accepted and preserved in raw interaction data. Validation is deliberately limited to the frozen public schema; upstream validation prose is not emulated (§10.5, §39.2).

state.description: Required. JSON string, object, or array. Never semantically interpreted by the core.

model.description: Required JSON string. v1 does not require it to appear in /v1/models; an arbitrary model string is allowed and is echoed by default (§39.2, §13.6).

questions.description: Required object with at least one property. Question entries are validated in lexicographic question-name order, after state, model, and questions themselves (§39.2, C-JEV-003).

instructions.description: Never participates in matching (§40.5). May be string, object, array, or null.

criteria.description: Shape is determined by type: required non-empty object for choice, required non-empty array for score, optional for noul. Contents never participate in matching.

answers.description: Exactly the request question-name set — no missing answer, no extra answer (§13.4, §13.5).

usage.description: Exactly {input_tokens: 0, output_tokens: 0} unless the stub configured other non-negative integers (§13.6).

Answer.description: The type field must match the corresponding request question's type; types are never coerced, and a mismatch is a fake-server error (§13.1, §13.4, C-JEV-016).

legend.description: Score answers only. Always derived from the request criteria; a fixture MUST NOT supply one (§13.3).

probabilities.description: Generated one-hot when omitted, linearly interpolated for a fractional score, and validated against the request criteria when explicit (§13.2, §13.3).

ValidationError.description: The deterministic 422 envelope. It is the fake contract, not a clone of upstream framework wording (§39.3). Note what is deliberately absent: the body carries no fake_jev_* code. The failure code fake_jev_validation_error exists as a journal and verification classification (§21.2, §41.7, §41.9), but the wire body for a validation failure is this Jev-compatible detail envelope so that a real client's own error handling keeps working. A 422 is therefore journaled with error fake_jev_validation_error while the response body stays Jev-shaped.

x-fake-jev-routing.$comment: Routing is exact-path. This block records the rules that are easy to lose, because each one produces a journaled unknown_route failure rather than a redirect (§39.8, §44.16).
x-fake-jev-routing.note: GET /v1/models?x=1 is handled as /v1/models. GET /v1/models/, POST /v1/models, and GET /v1/systemone are all unknown data-plane routes returning 404 fake_jev_unknown_route, are journaled, and fail verification. fake-jev MUST NOT rely on an HTTP router's automatic slash redirect behavior.
